name: MD-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 10-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
First-term incumbent Olszewski with a large fundraising edge ($1.0M raised vs. $20K)
No independent polls or expert ratings; markets price a Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Olszewski: a D+10 district, incumbency, a Democratic-tilted environment, and a lopsided money advantage over Wallace, who has raised only about $20,000. Polymarket prices a Democratic win around 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected outside spending against Olszewski would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 2nd District leans Democratic by about ten points, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski is seeking re-election with the advantages that come with holding the seat. He has raised roughly $1.0 million and holds over $600,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about $20,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are active on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 95%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap makes this a Safe D race, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
